paper_metadata.title: Smart Vault Security in Banks: A Quantum AI-Enabled Intrusion Detection System

summary: The paper proposes a hybrid QSVM-based intrusion detection system for bank smart vaults using quantum feature encoding and simulated quantum kernels. On a dataset experiment including a synthetic set of 1000 samples with 50 features, the system reports 96.5% accuracy, 95.2% precision, 97.0% recall, F1-score 97.5%, ROC-AUC 0.98, and ~0.015 s per-sample processing time, outperforming a classical SVM baseline by about 4–6% in accuracy-related metrics.

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical intrusion detection for smart vault security using quantum feature encoding, quantum kernel computation, and QSVM classification on a real-world bank vault security dataset.

algorithm.variant: Quantum kernel-based SVM (QSVM) for intrusion detection

hyperparameters.feature_encoding: parameterized quantum circuit with rotation gates
hyperparameters.kernel: quantum kernel based on squared inner product of quantum states

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical features are mapped to quantum states using a parameterized unitary U(x); implementation example uses a single-qubit rotation gate for feature encoding. The paper also mentions amplitude encoding in the system description, but the concrete algorithmic implementation shown is rotation-gate-based feature encoding.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary classification of normal vs intrusion events using QSVM decision function sign(sum_i alpha_i y_i K(x_i, x_new) + b)

problem_instance.description: Smart vault intrusion detection from multimodal banking security data including access logs, biometric data, sensor readings, and network traffic indicators.
problem_instance.dataset_name: Bank smart vault security dataset (real-world dataset; unnamed)

dataset_specification.description: Records labeled normal or intrusion; example features include time interval between access attempts, authentication score, sensor anomaly score, and network traffic indicators.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Missing values imputed using mean imputation; features normalized to [0,1]; preprocessing includes cleaning and normalization; real-time pipeline also mentions data cleaning and normalization before encoding.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Test-set evaluation on real-world dataset; additional simulations on a synthetic dataset of 1000 samples with 50 features per sample; metrics reported include accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC, and processing time per sample. No cross-validation protocol specified beyond C optimization.

hardware.classical_solver: scikit-learn SVM with custom quantum kernel

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Mean imputation; normalization to [0,1]; feature selection/extraction mentioned in algorithmic description.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Alert generation and response triggering upon intrusion detection; logging of incidents.

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports empirical performance improvements over a classical SVM baseline, but does not provide a quantified computational speedup or asymptotic advantage.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not specified; the work computes a quantum kernel using a statevector simulator with no resource estimates for scaling to real QPUs.
limiting_factors: All experiments executed on noiseless classical statevector simulation rather than quantum hardware
Quantum kernel evaluation performed by classical simulation so no demonstrated computational speed advantage
